summary: Multiple factual inaccuracies and style issues in the added Scaladoc for Future.Never and OnCompleteRunnable.

items.issue: The documentation claims the callback will never be executed because the future is never completed, but the implementation is `() => ()`, which is a no-op. This is correct, but the prose is misleading: it implies the callback is registered but never triggered, when in fact the implementation does nothing at all (not even registering). The behavior is correct, but the explanation is inaccurate.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'Does nothing. This future is never completed, so no callback is ever registered or executed.'

items.issue: The documentation states 'this method returns the future itself', but the return type is `Future[Throwable]`, while `this` is `Future[Nothing]`. The implementation returns `this`, which is a `Future[Nothing]`, but the return type is `Future[Throwable]`. This is a type mismatch in the prose.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'Returns a `Future[Throwable]` that is never completed, as this future is never completed.'

items.issue: The first overload of `transform` (with two functions) is documented as returning 'a new future with the transformed result', but the implementation returns `this`. The return type is `Future[S]`, but the behavior is to return the same `Future.Never` instance, not a new future. This is a factual inaccuracy.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'Since this future is never completed, this method returns the future itself.' (consistent with other methods)

items.issue: The second overload of `transform` (with a single function) has a `@param f` description that says 'the function to apply to the result of this future', but the parameter is of type `Try[Nothing] => Try[S]`. The description should clarify that it is a function applied to the `Try` result.
items.suggestion: Change `@param f` to: 'the function to apply to the `Try` result of this future'

items.issue: The `@return` tag states 'a new future with the transformed result', but the implementation returns `this`. This is a factual inaccuracy.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'Since this future is never completed, this method returns the future itself.'

items.issue: The `@return` tag states 'a future which will be completed with the result of the application of the function', but the implementation returns `this`. This is a factual inaccuracy.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'Since this future is never completed, this method returns the future itself.'

items.issue: The `@return` tag states 'a future which will be completed with the result of the application of the function', but the implementation returns `this`. This is a factual inaccuracy.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'Since this future is never completed, this method returns the future itself.'

items.issue: The `@return` tag states 'a future with the successful value of this future or the result of the partial function', but the implementation returns `this`. This is a factual inaccuracy.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'Since this future is never completed, this method returns the future itself.'

items.issue: The `@return` tag states 'a future with the successful value of this future or the outcome of the future returned by the partial function', but the implementation returns `this`. This is a factual inaccuracy.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'Since this future is never completed, this method returns the future itself.'

items.issue: The `@return` tag states 'a future with the results of both futures or the failure of the first of them that failed', but the implementation returns `this`. This is a factual inaccuracy.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'Since this future is never completed, this method returns the future itself.'

items.issue: The `@return` tag states 'a future with the successful result of this or that future or the failure of this future if both fail', but the implementation returns `this`. This is a factual inaccuracy.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'Since this future is never completed, this method returns the future itself.'

items.issue: The `@return` tag states 'a future which will be completed with the exact same outcome as this future but after the partial function has been executed', but the implementation returns `this`. This is a factual inaccuracy.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'Since this future is never completed, this method returns the future itself.'

items.issue: The `@tparam U` description 'only used to accept any return type of the given partial function' is awkward and not idiomatic Scaladoc.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'the return type of the partial function'

items.issue: The first sentence 'Returns a string representation of this future.' is redundant with the method name and could be more concise.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'A string representation of this future.'

items.issue: The first sentence 'A trait for runnables that can be batched together for more efficient execution.' is a fragment and does not stand alone well as an API-index summary.
items.suggestion: Change to: 'A trait for runnables that can be batched together for more efficient execution.' -> 'A trait for runnables that can be batched for more efficient execution.'
